question: The UK Government has admitted that carbon emissions from data centres could be 100 times greater than previously thought. Revised analysis accompanying a government ‘Compute Roadmap’ shows that UK greenhouse gas emissions from artificial intelligence (AI) could reach 123 million metric tonnes of CO2 (MtCO2), the equivalent of 3.4 percent of the UK’s emissions, between 2025 and 2035.

That is significantly higher than a forecast published in July 2025 of up to 0.142 MtCO2 from AI in 2035. The initial modelling was withdrawn in March in order to ‘reflect new analysis’. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission wish to also update its reply to my parliamentary question E004535/20251?
Does the Commission expect that it will be possible for the EU to remain competitive in the AI sector while maintaining all the EU’s emissions targets?
